title: Lab 201
text:
Lab 201 is the Poultry Breeding and Genetics Laboratory at National Chung Hsing University. Our work focuses on the genetic characterization, conservation, improvement of poultry through quantitative genetics, genomic selection as well as molecular genetic techniques.
We combine classical breeding theory with modern genomic tools to understand and improve traits of economic and biological importance in poultry.

title: BLUPF90 Documentation
text: This page collects the official documentation for the BLUPF90 family of programs. These files are provided by the BLUPF90 development team at the University of Georgia (UGA) and are made available here for the convenience of students in this course.

Start with the tutorial if you are new to BLUPF90. It walks you through a complete analysis from start to finish.

In this lecture, we introduce the concept of genomic selection and the data that makes it possible. We begin by defining what genomic data is and what it looks like in practice from SNP chips and genotype matrices to the marker maps that describe them. We then cover the fundamentals of quality control (QC) for genomic data, including the common filters applied to markers and samples before any analysis, and why these steps are essential for producing reliable genomic predictions.

title: Special Topics in Animal Selection
text:
A short introduction of the programs is provided by Yutaka Masuda at https://masuday.github.io/blupf90_tutorial/introduction_short.html#short-introduction-to-blupf90-programs.
Briefly as quoted from his text “BLUPF90 is the name of the software. It is also the name of a collection of programs derived from BLUPF90. In the latter case, we will refer to it as the BLUPF90 family or BLUPF90 programs. A concise description can also be found on the official wiki at the University of Georgia (http://nce.ads.uga.edu/wiki/doku.php).

BLUPF90 family of programs is a collection of software in Fortran 90/95 for mixed model computations in animal breeding. The goal of the software is to be as simple as with a matrix package and as efficient as in a programming language.

The BLUPF90 program creates and solves mixed model equations. It supports various models including the animal model, maternal model, and random regression model with multiple traits. The BLUPF90 family includes several programs for variance component estimation using REML and Gibbs sampling with various models. The set of programs is available on the official website (http://nce.ads.uga.edu) and can be freely used for academic or research purposes.”

section: 2.5 Download and Run BLUPF90 family of programs
text:
2.5 Download and Run BLUPF90 family of programs
For the best and up-to-date method of installing the software please visit the official BLUPF90 website.
No special installation procedure is required. Just download the program from the official website. Then, change the file permissions using chmod, for example, chmod 755 or chmod u+x (a helpful way to remember: ch_ange the mod_e to add execution permission +x for the _u_ser). You can move the program to your preferred directory, which may already be listed in your PATH environment variable. If not, you can create such a directory and move the program there.

2.5.1 OPTION 1. Recommended
File blupf90_win.zip contains Windows executables + GNUPLOT; an included script file sets access to all binaries and the graphing package. At this time, the best compiler appears to be from Intel; it is free for noncommercial use in Linux.
download the programs from the above link and store them in any D drive folder of your choice.

after installing MobaXterm and having dowloaded the file here is an example of how you can install the files.

Copy the files to your working directory on your D drive
Open MobaXterm >> Sessions >> WSL


Navigate to your working directory. When you open MobaXterm, you’ll see something like:
(base) sersam@SAM:/$


To navigate to your blup folder in D drive if you have not created it, create it first:
then inside WSL move back to the root folder and then navigate to your folder

cd ../..
cd /mnt/d/blup/



Navigate through sub-directories to find the executable. Use cd to move through folders until you reach the bin directory
Example:
cd blupf90_win/blupf90_win/bin/
List files to verify you’re in the right directory
ls
You should see executables like:
airemlf90.exe blupf90.exe renumf90.exe etc.
Move back one directory level
cd ..
Make all programs in the bin directory executable
chmod +x bin/
chmod 755 bin/
Verify the programs are now executable by testing one
renumf90 --help
Create a directory for binaries in your home directory
mkdir -p ~/bin
Move the programs to your binary directory
mv bin/* ~/bin
Add the binary directory to your PATH (optional but recommended)
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc



2.5.2 OPTION 2: Download programs individually
download the programs from here and store them in one folder. https://nce.ads.uga.edu/html/projects/programs/Linux/64bit/


Download programs from: https://nce.ads.uga.edu/html/projects/programs/Linux/64bit/

Download all required executables (e.g., renumf90, blupf90, airemlf90, etc.) and store them in a single folder

Navigate to the folder containing the downloaded programs
cd /path/to/your/downloaded/programs
List files to verify all programs are present
ls
Make all programs executable
chmod +x *
Create a directory for binaries in your home directory
mkdir -p ~/bin
Move all programs to the binary directory
mv * ~/bin
Check if ~/bin is in your PATH
echo $PATH
If ~/bin is not in your PATH, add it
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
Verify installation by testing a program
renumf90 --help



2.5.3 OPTION 3: Direct installation from BLUPF90 website
The BLUPF90 website also has the following method for the installation

Download the program (you can use wget or other tools like curl)
wget http://nce.ads.uga.edu/html/projects/programs/Mac_OSX/new/blupf90

Alternative using curl:
curl -O http://nce.ads.uga.edu/html/projects/programs/Mac_OSX/new/blupf90

Change the permission to make it executable
chmod 755 blupf90
chmod +x blupf90
Create a directory for binaries, if it doesn’t exist
mkdir -p ~/bin
Move the program to that directory
mv blupf90 ~/bin
Check if ~/bin directory is in your PATH environment variable
echo $PATH
If ~/bin is not in your PATH, add it (optional but recommended)
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
Verify the installation was successful
blupf90 --help



2.5.4 OPTION 4. The basic procedure.
A basic procedure to run the program which might work for this lecture in particular but for larger (not big) data sets it might not be compatible is as follows:

Download the program and save it in a folder.
(You may optionally add the folder to your system PATH. If you’re unsure what this is, you can skip this step.)
Save the required files in the same folder.
Open the Command Prompt and use the cd command to change to the folder’s directory.
Type the name of the program (e.g., blupf90 or blupf90.exe) to launch it.
When prompted, type the name of the parameter file. Some programs may ask for additional input.
Wait for the analysis to complete.
Check and collect the results.

If the program runs successfully, it will ask you for the name of the parameter file with the following prompt:
 name of parameter file?

2.6 Enhanced editor for Windows users
Common text editors include Notepad (Windows), TextEdit (macOS), and vi, Emacs, or nano (Linux/Unix). These are the default editors on each system, but you can install other editors for convenience. Notepad, in particular, has too few features to be practical in many cases. There are many free, powerful text editors available for Windows and other platforms.
Below are several well-known and free text editors. Some of them are multi-platform and support Linux, macOS, and Windows. Try a few and choose the one that suits you best:

Notepad++ (https://notepad-plus-plus.org) — Windows only
SciTE (http://www.scintilla.org/SciTE.html) — Windows
Visual Studio Code (https://code.visualstudio.com) — All platforms
